gate_count_source: 14 OMIQ filterContainers → 8 logical steps (co-plot gates merged)

steps.note: Ir: DNA1+ (Iridium-191 intercalator labels nucleated events; FCS channel PnN=Ir191Di, PnS=DNA1). This is the first cleanup gate — the Bjornson workflow skips the usual Helios Gaussian-discrimination cascade (Center/Offset/Residual/Width) and goes directly from raw FCS to DNA × Event_length. The gate selects nucleated events on DNA1+ without explicit Event_length filtering in this workflow — Event_length is shown on the y-axis primarily as a visualization context, and doublet/debris exclusion is effectively handled by the DNA1+ polygon shape and downstream marker-based gates. Note: Ir-intercalator labels both live and dead nucleated cells (dead cells often bind more intercalator due to increased membrane permeability), so this gate selects nucleated events but is NOT a viability gate.

CD45: CD45+ DNA2+ with DNA2++ excluded (leukocyte common antigen; all white blood cells, with DNA2 confirming intact nuclei; FCS PnN=Ir193Di/In115Di, PnS=DNA2/CD45_In115Di). The polygon intentionally excludes the DNA2-hyperbright tail — events with aberrantly high DNA2 signal are most consistent with doublets/aggregates or damaged/hyperploid nuclei and are removed here. This gate is per-file adjusted in OMIQ (perFileFilters on 58 of 512 samples) because CD45-In115 signal intensity varies by acquisition run — polygon is redrawn per sample for samples that drift from the template. Important caveat: this panel has no live/dead discriminator (no cisplatin/rhodium), and the DNA1 ∩ DNA2 gate selects nucleated intact events rather than specifically live cells. Downstream populations may therefore include a mixture of live and dead leukocytes. Useful co-markers for cleaner leukocyte gating: CD235a_In113Di (glycophorin A) flags erythrocyte-leukocyte aggregates — bona fide leukocytes should be CD235a-; CD61_Ce140Di (platelet GPIIIa) flags platelet-leukocyte aggregates — bona fide leukocytes should be CD61-. Both are in panel but not used in this workflow; they can serve as QC checks on the CD45+ population.

Granulocyte: CD45low/int CD66+ (neutrophils and eosinophils; neutrophils typically show CD45 low-to-intermediate and dominate this gate). Note that basophils express CD66 at very low levels and are generally NOT captured in a CD66+ granulocyte gate — they fall into the CD3-/CD19-/HLA-DR-/CD7- residual at Step 6 instead. CD45hiCD66lo: CD45hi CD66- (mononuclear fraction — lymphocytes, monocytes, DCs, NK). This is the main myeloid/lymphoid split. Useful co-markers: CD16_Tb159Di further confirms neutrophils within Granulocyte (neutrophils CD16+, eosinophils CD16-); CD11b_Eu153Di is positive on both neutrophils and eosinophils and reinforces granulocyte identity; CD33_Nd142Di (pan-myeloid) is typically low-to-intermediate on granulocytes vs higher on monocytes and can help distinguish myeloid vs lymphoid within the CD45hiCD66lo fraction; HLA-DR_Yb176Di is negative on granulocytes, providing a negative-marker confirmation; CD3_Gd157Di / CD19_Yb173Di low confirms non-lymphoid nature of CD45hiCD66lo minor populations.

Three-way lymphoid split on a single CD3 × CD19 plot. Bcells: CD3- CD19+ (B lymphocytes). Tcells: CD3+ CD19- (T lymphocytes — both αβ and γδ; TCR subtypes not resolved in this panel). CD3negCD19neg: CD3- CD19- (NK cells, ILCs, monocytes, DCs, basophils — parsed downstream). Useful co-markers: CD20 (not in panel) would refine mature B cells; CD56_Lu175Di resolves NK from other CD3-CD19- subsets downstream; IgM_Yb174Di (in panel) could further refine mature vs naive B cells; HLA-DR_Yb176Di is expressed on B cells (APCs) and typically negative on resting T cells — useful as a positive confirmation for Bcells and a negative check for Tcells; CD7_Pr141Di is expressed on essentially all T cells (and NK) but not on B cells, reinforcing Tcells assignment within the CD3+CD19- polygon.

CD4Tcells: CD4+ CD8- (helper T cells). CD8Tcells: CD4- CD8+ (cytotoxic T cells). Double-positive (DPT) and double-negative (DNT, includes MAIT/NKT) subsets are NOT explicitly gated in this workflow — they fall outside both polygon regions and are not tracked. Useful co-markers: CD45RA_Er166Di / CCR7_Yb171Di enable memory subset analysis (Naive/TCM/TEM/TEMRA) — present in panel but not gated in this simplified workflow. FoxP3_Er167Di (in panel) would resolve Treg within CD4Tcells; CD161_Er168Di (in panel) would mark MAIT within the unassigned DNT residual; CD7_Pr141Di confirms T cell identity across both CD4 and CD8 subsets (expressed on >95% of mature T cells); CD56_Lu175Di (in panel) would identify NKT within DPT/DNT residuals.

Within the CD3-CD19- residual, CD7 × HLA-DR separates NK (CD7+, lymphoid) from myeloid APCs (HLA-DR+). NKcells: CD7+ HLA-DR- (CD7 is expressed on most NK cells — strongly on CD56bright NK, more variably on CD56dim NK subsets; HLA-DR- excludes APCs). HLA-DRposCD7neg: HLA-DR+ CD7- (antigen-presenting cells: monocytes, DCs — further parsed downstream). The CD7- HLA-DR- quadrant (unlabeled) contains basophils and any remaining residual. Useful co-markers: CD56_Lu175Di is the classical NK marker and serves as a sanity check — most NK are CD56+; CD16_Tb159Di marks cytotoxic mature NK (CD56dim CD16+); CD161_Er168Di is expressed on NK cells (particularly CD56bright subset) and provides additional NK confirmation; CD123_Nd148Di is useful for identifying basophils in the unlabeled CD7-HLA-DR- residual quadrant (basophils are CD123+ HLA-DR- CD7-), though basophils are not explicitly gated in this workflow; CD33_Nd142Di is typically higher on the HLA-DR+CD7- myeloid fraction and low on NK, reinforcing the split.

Monocytes: CD11b+ (any CD16) OR CD11b- CD16+ — the polygon captures both the CD11b+ region (classical, intermediate, and most non-classical monocytes) AND the CD11b-low CD16+ region to include non-classical monocyte populations that have down-regulated CD11b. The standard Ziegler-Heitbrock nomenclature defines classical CD14++CD16-, intermediate CD14++CD16+, and non-classical CD14+CD16++ subsets on a CD14 × CD16 plot, but this workflow does not split them. CD11bnegCD16neg: CD11b- CD16- (non-monocyte APC residual — enriches for DCs, resolved at Step 8). Useful co-markers: CD14_Eu151Di confirms monocyte identity and would enable classical/intermediate/non-classical subset splitting on CD14 × CD16 if needed; CD33_Nd142Di is a pan-myeloid marker — monocytes are CD33++ (higher than DCs or granulocytes), providing strong positive confirmation; HLA-DR_Yb176Di is positive on monocytes (already enforced by parent chain) and can distinguish them from CD16+ NK contamination if any leaks through; CD11c_Nd143Di is also expressed on monocytes (in addition to cDCs), useful as a secondary myeloid marker.

DCs: CD11c+ AND/OR CD123+ (total dendritic cells — conventional cDC are CD11c+ CD123-, plasmacytoid pDC are CD11c- CD123+; this gate captures both with a single polygon). cDC vs pDC subtypes are NOT split in this workflow. Useful co-markers: HLA-DR+ is a DC hallmark and already enforced by the upstream parent chain; CD1c_Dy162Di and BDCA3_Dy164Di (BDCA3/CD141) are available in panel and would resolve cDC1 (BDCA3+) vs cDC2 (CD1c+) if needed; CD33_Nd142Di confirms myeloid lineage (cDCs are CD33+, lower than monocytes); CD14_Eu151Di should be negative/low on DCs — useful as a negative check to exclude residual monocytes that leaked past Step 7; CD11b_Eu153Di is generally low/negative on DCs (already enforced by parent being CD11b- CD16-), distinguishing them from monocytes.
